sources.note: 17 V.S.A. section 2646 establishes the office (towns elect a moderator for a one-year term); no official source publishes the current holder, so the post is created without a membership

Town of Salisbury, Warning for the Annual Town Meeting (floor meeting February 28, 2026; Australian ballot March 3, 2026): Article 4 elects a Moderator for a one-year term; no official source publishes the 2026 outcome
24 App. V.S.A. ch. 146 (Town of Salisbury): section 2: the Town Clerk is elected for a one-year term
Town of Salisbury, Warning for the Annual Town Meeting (floor meeting February 28, 2026; Australian ballot March 3, 2026): Article 4 elects a Town Clerk for a one-year term; no tally is published
Town of Salisbury, Town Clerk page (townofsalisbury.org), as read October 19, 2026: Fred Kenney is the Town Clerk

Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, town clerk contact spreadsheet (updated June 12, 2026): names Allen Hathaway as Salisbury's Town Clerk (June 2026); the January 2026 Guide names him as well, and the town's clerk page still named him in June 2026. Hathaway held the office through June 2026 and Kenney succeeded him afterward; Kenney is recorded as an appointed successor on the disclosed inference that the Selectboard filled a vacancy (the Plainfield/Readsboro pattern). Hathaway, a departed holder, is not recorded
24 App. V.S.A. ch. 146 (Town of Salisbury): section 1: the Town Treasurer is appointed by the Selectboard to a one-year employment term (July 1 to June 30)
Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, 'Guide to Vermont's Town Clerks, Treasurers, and County Officials' (January 2026): lists Kerry Dashnaw as Salisbury's Town Treasurer

Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, 'Vermont Selectboard Members' directory (updated June 5, 2026): lists Salisbury's five selectboard members: Patrick Dunn (Chair), Jonathan Blake (Vice Chair), Robbie Devoid, Mark Gleason, and Susan Mackey

Town of Salisbury official website (townofsalisbury.org): the selectboard pages name the same five members. Jonathan Blake is styled a former state representative on the town's volunteers page; the sitting Addison-4 representatives are Herb Olson and Karen Lueders, and Blake is minted new here

sources.note: Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, 'Vermont Justices of the Peace' listing (updated December 4, 2025): lists seven Salisbury justices of the peace: Jonathan Blake (as 'Jonathon Blake'), Brian Christie, Jaclyn Davidson, Jeff McDonough, David Moats, Kathryn Schloff, and Susan Scott. This Jeff McDonough is a Salisbury resident, a different man from the Town of Leicester's first constable of the same name
